events.what: Klurman, Shparlinski and Teräväinen prove unconditionally that the Artin asymptotic holds for almost all a up to exp((log log x)^2)
Goldmakher, Martin and Peringuey propose refined conjectures on the distribution of ord_p(a), proved under GRH, with weaker unconditional versions
Murty and Naik prove Artin's conjecture conditional on a new, unproven non-abelian large sieve inequality

judgement.doubts: The competing_reading's 'partial' argument fails: 'almost all a up to exp((log log x)^2)' lets the exceptional set move with x, so it establishes the conjecture for no fixed a; it is an average/proportion result, i.e. a bound, not a case. Murty–Naik is a reduction to an unproven inequality (scope none), like Hooley's GRH result. Whether KST even counts as progress on this bullet rather than none is arguable; kept as progress. FrontierMath item is a variant benchmark, not an event.

outcome_prefix: Status rests on Klurman–Shparlinski–Teräväinen (arXiv:2412.13355, Dec 2024, published in Bull. LMS): an unconditional almost-all-a average result, a bound on the open question; the Murty–Naik conditional proof is a reduction and cannot set the status.

corrections.why: F8: the record says Murty–Naik is conditional on an inequality 'that is itself an open conjecture', a reduction (scope none) that cannot set the status; the progress status rests on the KST average result.

corrections.from: Murty, Naik, Goldmakher, Martin, Peringuey, Klurman, Shparlinski, Teräväinen
corrections.why: F8: credited_humans describe the event the status rests on; GMP is a variant and Murty–Naik a conditional reduction.
other: kept despite competing_reading's partial case; the almost-all statement has an x-dependent exceptional set and settles no fixed a, so it is a bound/proportion, not a case.
